knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Triple Integral Using a Change of Variables

question.:question/problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u=2 x + 2 y,\quad v=y - 2 z,\quad w=4 z
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
\iiint_R \left(\left(2 x + 2 y\right) \left(y - 2 z\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}V,
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z):0\le 2 x + 2 y\le 3,\quad 0\le y - 2 z\le 2,\quad 0\le z\le 3\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=2 x + 2 y,\quad v=y - 2 z,\quad w=4 z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v,w):0\le u\le 3,\quad 0\le v\le 2,\quad 0\le w\le 12\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)\left(\left(2\right)\cdot \left(1\right)-\left(2\right)\cdot \left(0\right)\right) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=\frac{1}{8}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R \left(\left(2 x + 2 y\right) \left(y - 2 z\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta \left(u v\right)\cdot \left|\frac{1}{8}\right|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\iiint_\Delta \left(\frac{u v}{8}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{2}\int_{0}^{12}\left(\frac{u v}{8}\right)\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{2}\left(\left[\frac{u v w}{8}\right]_{w=0}^{w=12}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{2}\left(\left(\frac{u v \left(12\right)}{8}\right)-\left(\frac{u v \left(0\right)}{8}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{2}\left(\left(\frac{3 u v}{2}\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{2}\left(\frac{3 u v}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left[\frac{3 u v^{2}}{4}\right]_{v=0}^{v=2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left(\frac{3 u \left(2\right)^{2}}{4}\right)-\left(\frac{3 u \left(0\right)^{2}}{4}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left(3 u\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\left(3 u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\left[\frac{3 u^{2}}{2}\right]_{u=0}^{u=3} \\  & =\left(\frac{3 \left(3\right)^{2}}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{3 \left(0\right)^{2}}{2}\right) \\  & =\left(\frac{27}{2}\right)-\left(0\right) \\  & =\frac{27}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Triple Integral Using a Change of Variables

question.:question/problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u=x + y^{2},\quad v=y + z,\quad w=4 z
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
\iiint_R \left(\left(y + z\right) e^{x + y^{2}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}V,
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z):1\le x + y^{2}\le 3,\quad 1\le y + z\le 3,\quad 1\le z\le 3\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x + y^{2},\quad v=y + z,\quad w=4 z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v,w):1\le u\le 3,\quad 1\le v\le 3,\quad 4\le w\le 12\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 y & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 y \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(4\right)\left(\left(1\right)\cdot \left(1\right)-\left(2 y\right)\cdot \left(0\right)\right) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R \left(\left(y + z\right) e^{x + y^{2}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta \left(v e^{u}\right)\cdot \left|\frac{1}{4}\right|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\iiint_\Delta \left(\frac{v e^{u}}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{3}\int_{4}^{12}\left(\frac{v e^{u}}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{3}\left(\left[\frac{v w e^{u}}{4}\right]_{w=4}^{w=12}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{3}\left(\left(\frac{v \left(12\right) e^{u}}{4}\right)-\left(\frac{v \left(4\right) e^{u}}{4}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{3}\left(\left(3 v e^{u}\right)-\left(v e^{u}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\int_{1}^{3}\left(2 v e^{u}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\left(\left[v^{2} e^{u}\right]_{v=1}^{v=3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\left(\left(\left(3\right)^{2} e^{u}\right)-\left(\left(1\right)^{2} e^{u}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\left(\left(9 e^{u}\right)-\left(e^{u}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{1}^{3}\left(8 e^{u}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\left[8 e^{u}\right]_{u=1}^{u=3} \\  & =\left(8 e^{\left(3\right)}\right)-\left(8 e^{\left(1\right)}\right) \\  & =\left(8 e^{3}\right)-\left(8 e\right) \\  & =- 8 e \left(- e^{2} + 1\right)\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u=x + y^{2},\quad v=y + 2 z,\quad w=3 z
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
\iiint_R \left(\left(y + 2 z\right) e^{x + y^{2}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}V,
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z):0\le x + y^{2}\le 3,\quad 0\le y + 2 z\le 3,\quad 0\le z\le 2\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x + y^{2},\quad v=y + 2 z,\quad w=3 z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v,w):0\le u\le 3,\quad 0\le v\le 3,\quad 0\le w\le 6\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 y & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(3\right)(-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 y \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(3\right)\left(\left(1\right)\cdot \left(1\right)-\left(2 y\right)\cdot \left(0\right)\right) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R \left(\left(y + 2 z\right) e^{x + y^{2}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta \left(v e^{u}\right)\cdot \left|\frac{1}{3}\right|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\iiint_\Delta \left(\frac{v e^{u}}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{6}\left(\frac{v e^{u}}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left[\frac{v w e^{u}}{3}\right]_{w=0}^{w=6}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left(\frac{v \left(6\right) e^{u}}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{v \left(0\right) e^{u}}{3}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left(2 v e^{u}\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{3}\left(2 v e^{u}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left[v^{2} e^{u}\right]_{v=0}^{v=3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left(\left(3\right)^{2} e^{u}\right)-\left(\left(0\right)^{2} e^{u}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\left(\left(9 e^{u}\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\int_{0}^{3}\left(9 e^{u}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\left[9 e^{u}\right]_{u=0}^{u=3} \\  & =\left(9 e^{\left(3\right)}\right)-\left(9 e^{\left(0\right)}\right) \\  & =\left(9 e^{3}\right)-\left(9\right) \\  & =-9 + 9 e^{3}\end{aligned}
$$
